text:
ash: FYI I pushed the new prefix-inspectops dashboard to grafana-prod just now. It's meant to combine per-model / per-route / per-customer hit-rate + token-saved waterfall. Please skim for obvious regressions. :eyes:

maria: saw it, looks nice. Quick question — the token-saved numbers look much lower for model-rw-2 on /chat/assistant between 13:00-14:00 UTC. Is that a dashboard bug or a real drop?

metrics-bot: alert: prefix_cache_agg.drop_pct > 15% for route=/chat/assistant model=model-rw-2 window=13:05-13:20 UTC. Documentation: https://internal.grafana/prefix-inspectops

devon: confirmed a drop in hit-rate in the raw timeseries (per-tenant slice). The drop aligns with an autoscaler churn event in dedicated pools. Could be warmup keying + kernel bump interaction.

ash: @devon good catch. Do we have profiling from the 13:00 window? I want to know if batching heuristics changed effective latency and prevented proper KV cache warmup.

sandeep: I pulled a short profile dump. Two notable things: (1) kernel selection moved to the new fused-simd path for this model at 12:55 due to recent rollout, and that path reduces micro-batch size tolerance. (2) batching heuristic fallback threshold tightened so requests got more spread into smaller batches. Combined, KV-key prefetch didn't hit as often.

matt: sharing the query I used to recreate token-saved waterfall (we run this hourly):

```
SELECT
  route,
  model,
  tenant_id,
  time_bucket('1m', ts) as minute,
  sum(tokens_saved) as tokens_saved,
  avg(prefix_hitrate) as hr
FROM prefix_cache_events
WHERE ts >= now() - interval '2 hours'
GROUP BY route, model, tenant_id, minute
ORDER BY minute;
```

maria: thanks. I pulled the tenant slice for AcmeCorp — their hit-rate fell from 72%->41% in that interval and token-saved dropped ~38%. AcmeCorp uses long prefixes so they're sensitive to any kernel/batching regressions.

devon: note: the kernel rollout had a guardrail but the canary window overlapped with an autoscaler policy change we pushed at 12:58. Two independent changes that both reduce aggregated batch sizes = fewer shared prefixes in a batch -> lower observed hit-rate.

ash: action items: (1) rollback kernel fused-simd on model-rw-2 for now, (2) revert batching threshold change, (3) re-run the dashboard for 13:00-14:00 to confirm recovery, (4) add an annotation layer to grafana for kernel/batching rollouts so we can correlate automatically.

sandeep: I'll create the rollback PR for the kernel and add an explicit metric that emits effective micro-batch_size distribution per-node. That will help detect this earlier.

matt: I'll add an annotation stream from our rollout service into grafana and wire an alert that watches token-saved delta > 20% for top-10 tenants.

maria: small UX ask — can we add a toggled breakdown on the dashboard that shows per-customer contribution to token-saved (so SREs can flip to "top contributors" quickly)? Right now the default view hides tenant-level churn.

ash: yes, please add that. Also add a compact timeline that overlays kernel path vs batching fallback % vs hit-rate. That triple view would make root-cause obvious.

metrics-bot: note: automated backfill scheduled to recompute tokens_saved for 13:00-14:00 after any rollbacks. Status will post here when done.

devon: quick suggestion for keying: we saw some key variance where sequence-boundary hashing returned different keys after a small tokenizer change in canary. If we include a short fingerprint (first-8hash) column on dashboard, we can spot key drift vs true workload change.

sandeep: good idea. I'll add fingerprint column to the event stream and join in the dashboard panels.

matt: ok, rolling out annotation + tenant toggle + micro-batch histogram this afternoon. I'll ping when live.

ash: thanks everyone. We'll monitor. If anyone sees continued token-saved delta after rollback, escalate to incident channel. :thumbsup:
